en.title: Painters and composers
en.summary: Art and music from the English-speaking world, and the language of describing a picture.

paragraphs: Looking at a picture or listening to a piece of music, we describe and guess. This lesson presents artists and composers and practises modal verbs of deduction.

William Hogarth painted scenes of London life in the eighteenth century, while J. M. W. Turner, whose paintings of storms and sunsets seem almost abstract, changed landscape painting in the nineteenth. John Constable painted the countryside of Suffolk. In the United States, Edward Hopper painted lonely city scenes, and Georgia O'Keeffe painted flowers and desert landscapes. In music, Henry Purcell wrote opera in the seventeenth century, and George Frideric Handel, who was born in Germany but lived in London from 1712, composed Messiah in 1741. Edward Elgar wrote Pomp and Circumstance, played at the Last Night of the Proms, and in America George Gershwin joined jazz and classical music in Rhapsody in Blue (1924).

paragraphs: **1. Modals of deduction express how sure you are.** Must is almost certain, may or might is possible, can't is impossible. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
CertaintyExample
must (very sure)It must be a storm at sea.
might (possible)It might be Turner.
can't (impossible)It can't be a photograph.

paragraphs: **2. Past deduction uses have and a participle.** See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses.

blocks.html:
PresentPast
It must be old.It must have been painted in 1830.
He might be famous.He might have been a teacher.

items: A **landscape** shows scenery; a **portrait** shows a person.
A **composer** writes music; a **conductor** leads the orchestra.

paragraphs: The Last Night of the Proms in London is a concert in which the audience sings along to patriotic songs, which has become a tradition.
